title: Introduce pipelined attention kernel with async prefetch and KV-slab cache; fused rotary pass
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Motivation: several production workloads exhibit tail latency and throughput sensitivity when sequence lengths vary and when cold KV-cache misses occur. This change implements a pipelined attention kernel that overlaps QKV compute with async prefetch of KV slabs, adds a compact slab-based KV cache to reduce lookup overhead, and introduces a fused rotary/rope transformation pass at the kernel level. The implementation is opt-in behind a runtime feature flag (ATTN_PIPELINE=on) and includes a compatibility fallback to the existing attention path for models that rely on nonstandard rotary encodings. Highlights: 1) New pipelined kernel that splits the attention op into (a) gather + rotary-fuse compute for Q/K/V, (b) async DMA prefetch of KV slab pages based on predicted access windows, and (c) overlap of softmax/weighted-sum with next-token KV assembly. This reduces blocking on device memory stalls and improves token throughput for batched streaming. 2) KV-slab cache: a compact page-aligned slab cache with LRU eviction tuned for typical prefix reuse patterns and continuous-batching workloads. The cache exposes lightweight instrumentation hooks for hit/miss histograms and integrates with existing prefix-KV eviction policies. 3) Fused rotary pass: a compute-level fusion that applies rotary embeddings immediately after Q/K compute and before layout transposition to reduce memory traffic and kernel launches. 4) Scheduler hints for continuous batching: the runtime receives a short-lived hint from the kernel (prefetch latency and observed reuse window) which the scheduler uses to slightly bias batch formation and placement to improve coalesced KV usage. 5) Safety and fallbacks: if async prefetch is not supported on the device or if the slab cache pressure exceeds thresholds, the runtime falls back to the legacy attention kernel. Tests and validation: microbenchmarks (redwood/benchmarks/attn_pipeline) show median latency improvements of 18-26% and throughput +20-35% on production-like GPT-style models across sequence lengths 128..1024 with minimal memory overhead (+1-3%). CI and canary: added unit tests, end-to-end regression tests, and a staged perf-canary rollout plan (perf-canary config included) to gradually enable the flag for Dedicated customers. Related Linear issues: ENG-3421 (attention perf), ENG-3490 (kv cache telemetry). This PR bundles codegen patches, kernel implementations, runtime plumbing, and documentation for the runtime config. See commits and file list below for specifics.
